analysis: What changed vs the 4 AM brief: the selloff is deepening, not stabilizing. At 4:32 AM ET Nasdaq futures were -2.22%; by ~7:07 AM ET they were -3.03%, with the S&P at -2.02% and the Dow at -1.35%. The VIX has jumped to 29.04 (+10.17% on the day) from 26.36 in the prior brief. Monday's Huang rally is now fully erased for AI hardware: the ten largest AI hardware names are down 5.1% on average premarket and sit 1.0% below their Friday closes — Nvidia is the exception only because its Monday gain was so large (+31.5%). The rout went global overnight: KOSPI -6.16%, Nikkei -2.78%, Shanghai -2.03%, with SK Hynix -11% and SoftBank -14.8%. Deere added a cyclical leg to the story, missing EPS and guiding FY27 net income to $4.5-5.25B vs ~$5.9B expected, down ~3% premarket. The tariff catalyst remains unresolved: as of ~6 AM ET the USTR had still not posted findings or rates, so the market is selling the headline, not the details. Dell (-6% premarket) and Workday (-9.9%) show the beat-and-fall pattern from Tuesday is still the rule. Signal vs noise: the accelerating futures slide, the VIX spike, the global chip rout and Deere's guide cut are signal; the exact premarket percentages and any single-name bounce are noise. The 8:30 AM ET data dump (PCE, Q3 GDP, durable goods, jobless claims) is now the deciding input into a thin Thanksgiving-week tape.

community_signals.takeaway: Discussion frames the Amodei family's $561M of IPO-window sales as insider caution at the top — the same selling the 4 AM brief flagged from Form 4 filings, now read by HN commenters as a confidence signal rather than routine diversification.

headlines.headline: Futures slide deepens into the open: as of ~7:07 AM ET, Nasdaq 100 futures -3.03%, S&P 500 futures -2.02%, Dow futures -1.35% — versus -2.22% / -1.31% / -0.75% at 4:32 AM ET. VIX jumped to 29.04, up 10.17% on the day.
headlines.why_it_matters: The gap-down is getting worse by the hour, not better — the open is set to start well below Tuesday's close with tech leading the downside and fear gauges spiking.

headlines.headline: Deere missed Q4 EPS ($3.89 vs ~$4.03-4.07 expected) on $10.51B net sales (above ~$10.38B expected) and guided FY27 net income to $4.5-5.25B, well below the ~$5.9B Wall Street expected. Large-ag sales fell 15%. Shares -2.7% to -3.5% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: A weak guide from a cyclical bellwether adds a demand-side leg to a selloff that was mostly about AI and tariffs — farm-economy pressure is now showing up in the numbers.

headlines.headline: Global AI rout overnight: South Korea's KOSPI plunged 6.16% (SK Hynix -11%, Samsung -9.9%), Japan's Nikkei -2.78%, Shanghai -2.03%; SoftBank -14.8%. Europe is holding up better (STOXX 600 -0.19%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI unwind is not a US-only move — Asian chip and AI names fell harder overnight, which keeps pressure on US chip and hyperscaler names into the open.

headlines.headline: AI hardware stocks have now erased Monday's Huang rally: the ten largest AI hardware names are down 5.1% on average in premarket trading and sit 1.0% below their Friday closes. Nvidia -5.0% at $147.60; Micron, AMD and Marvell each down more than 5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The reinstatement bounce is fully retraced for the group — earnings context: Nov 17, EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B vs $109.28B expected (+103% y/y). The overhangs (SEC probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Huang's Dec 1 House testimony) still dominate the tape.

headlines.headline: Mega-caps all red premarket: Alphabet -3.0%, Amazon -3.2%, Microsoft -1.9%, Meta -1.4% (updated from the 4 AM read).
headlines.why_it_matters: No mega-cap is escaping the slide, and the most AI-exposed hyperscalers are down most — the rotation-into-value pattern from Tuesday is intact but the whole tape is falling now.

headlines.headline: Dell -6% premarket despite raising its full-year revenue guide to $202B on a record quarter; Workday -9.9% after beating EPS but guiding Q4 subscription revenue light. The beat-and-fall pattern from Tuesday is continuing.
headlines.why_it_matters: Even a record quarter with a raised guide is being sold — the market is judging guidance and valuation, not the quarter, and the bar for AI-linked names stays high.

headlines.headline: No USTR tariff findings posted as of ~6 AM ET: the Section 301 probe findings and any new duty rates on the 16 trading partners are still unpublished, so the market is selling the headline, not the details.
headlines.why_it_matters: The tariff catalyst is still single-source and unconfirmed in substance — no rates or product lists exist yet, so any official posting before the open could move futures either way.

headlines.headline: Notable premarket movers outside tech: PNC Financial +5.4% and General Dynamics +3.7% higher; Carlisle -17.9% and Tradeweb -17.4% lower. No reasons were given in the sourced report.
headlines.why_it_matters: A few names are bucking the tape in both directions — defensive/financial strength versus sharp single-name drops — but without sourced reasons these are moves to note, not signals to chase.
